items.title: Effectiveness of Contextualized 5E Inquiry Modules in Enhancing Scientific Literacy and Conceptual Mastery among STE Learners
items.adviser: Dr. E. M. Santos, Ph.D. (Faculty of Education)
items.abstract: This study evaluated the pedagogical impact of localized 5E (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate) inquiry-based learning modules on Grade 7 STE students. Utilizing a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design (N=96), the research demonstrated statistically significant gains in higher-order thinking skills (HOTS) and conceptual retention compared to traditional lecture-demonstration methods (p < 0.01). Qualitative thematic analysis further indicated increased learner self-efficacy in formulating testable scientific questions.
items.methods: Quasi-experimental design, normalized Hake gain scores, ANCOVA, Likert-scale self-efficacy surveys, classroom observation protocols.
items.key_findings: Normalized learning gain (g = 0.68, medium-to-high effect size) in experimental sections; 38% increase in student engagement during investigative laboratory sessions.

items.title: Bio-coagulant Potential of Indigenous Moringa oleifera Seed Extracts in Turbid River Water Clarification
items.adviser: Ramelito Jr. C. Sanchez, LPT (Coaching Adviser)
items.abstract: Mentored a student research trio investigating sustainable water treatment alternatives for flood-prone riverine communities. Using standardized jar tests and turbidity nephelometry, the team quantified the coagulation efficiency of powdered Moringa seed extracts against synthetic alum.
items.methods: Standard jar testing, turbidity measurements (NTU), pH stabilization testing, microbial culture assays.
items.key_findings: Moringa seed coagulant achieved up to 92.4% turbidity reduction without destabilizing ambient water pH, offering a viable, non-toxic alternative to chemical coagulants.
